narrationScript:
Welcome to Cohortia's Computer Architecture course. In this first chapter, 'What Is Computer Architecture?', we'll lay the foundational understanding for the entire discipline. Computer architecture is the critical bridge connecting the abstract world of software with the tangible realm of hardware. It defines how processors are designed, how memory is organized, and how computational tasks are executed efficiently.

By the end of this module, you'll be able to distinguish between computer architecture, often referred to as the Instruction Set Architecture, and microarchitecture, which is its specific implementation. We'll explore the distinct roles of architecture, microarchitecture, and the underlying logic and technology in processor design. You'll also learn to identify the key metrics used to evaluate any computer architecture: performance, power, area, cost, and reliability. Finally, we'll understand the concept of the implementation stack and how decisions made at each level profoundly affect the others. Let's begin our exploration into the intricate world of computer architecture.
